title: storage: fix implicit directory sizes without relaxing mtime checks
body:
This PR is limited to the size fix. It preserves strict mtime checks and does not resolve the existing directory-mtime discrepancies.

English translation of the author's Chinese scope statement; translation assisted by AI.

```diff
-func newCheckDirectory(uid, gid int, size int64, mode os.FileMode, mtime int64) *checkDirectory
+func newCheckDirectory(uid, gid int, mode os.FileMode, mtime int64) *checkDirectory

-size:     size,
+size:     0,
```

```text
Changeset entry: etc/nested/payload, regular file, size=7
Implicit directories: etc/ and etc/nested/
Expected directory sizes: 0
Expected file size: 7

Unit tests: storage/check_test.go
Deleted: storage/check_implicit_directory_test.go
Overlay integration tests: storage/check_implicit_overlay_test.go (unchanged)
```

comments.body:
Thanks for the feedback. I agree that the directory-size invariant should be enforced by the constructor. I’ll remove the size parameter from newCheckDirectory, initialize it to zero internally, and move the focused regression test into storage/check_test.go.

The reason for the fix is that add() already normalizes non-regular entries to size zero, but implicitly created parent directories bypass that normalization: when processing a regular file such as etc/nested/payload with size 7, the missing parent directories inherit that 7.

I’ll include a before/after regression result showing that both parent directories have size zero while the regular file retains size 7. The timestamp checks remain unchanged.

Would that address the code-shape concerns and make the correctness review easier?

Updated in 261dab2: removed the constructor’s size parameter and moved the unit tests into storage/check_test.go. The regression test fails against the original code because both implicit parent directories inherit size 7, and passes with the fix. All 26 related test cases, including subtests, and go vet pass in a local Linux arm64 container. Timestamp checks remain unchanged.
